envelope.description: Characterise all three defects as failing baselines, as separate tests with declared inversion points

body.title: Characterise all three defects as failing baselines, as separate tests with declared inversion points
body.summary: Drive a standalone build through implement then validate against a throwaway git repo and capture the record AS IT IS TODAY, as EXPECTATIONS OF THE WRONG BEHAVIOUR, so every later task diffs against a baseline and the fix is proved by a red-to-green transition rather than asserted. s1 established the flip by reading code (c14); this makes it observable. The three defects invert at THREE DIFFERENT tasks, so they must be separately-named tests each naming its inversion point IN the test name: the lost '## Scope' inverts at t8 (the converged renderer emits Scope whenever body.focus is present, regardless of the flag), the forced meta.standalone false inverts at t9, and the empty change set inverts at t6. Treating them as one unit would make t8 look like a regression and invite the build to 'fix' it by reverting an improvement. MUST be first: written after any fix, it encodes the fixed behaviour and proves nothing.
acceptanceChecks: TEST A, named for its t8 inversion point: a standalone record driven through implement-then-validate renders md containing NO '## Scope' while the json still carries body.focus — the orphaned-content defect
TEST B, named for its t9 inversion point: the same run's persisted json has meta.standalone === false despite the implement write setting it true — the forced-flag defect
TEST C, named for its t6 inversion point: on a CLEAN working tree collectBuildChangeLog returns [] and the persisted record has no '## Changes' section
All three PASS on unmodified HEAD (they characterise, they do not yet demand), and each carries a comment naming the exact task that will invert it
The throwaway-repo harness follows the committed gate idiom at diff-grounding.test.ts:150 and asserts read-only afterwards via rev-list --count and status --porcelain

tests.name: CHARACTERISATION A (inverts at t8): a standalone build's persisted md contains NO '## Scope' while its json still carries body.focus
CHARACTERISATION B (inverts at t9): the shared validate persist forces meta.standalone to false despite implement writing true
CHARACTERISATION C (inverts at t6): a CLEAN working tree yields an empty changeLog and a record with no '## Changes' section
the characterisation harness is read-only — rev-list --count and status --porcelain unchanged afterwards — and the suite skips cleanly when git is unavailable
